text:
maria: RFC follow-up — sketching a minimal transport contract for iterator resume + retries across Python/TS/Go. TL;DR: opaque resume token, optional resume-offset, idempotency key for in-flight replay, server-declared replay window.

kevin: link to the RFC pls? will read.

maria: https://r.redwood/rfcs/transport-resume-v0 (draft) — main changes from previous: 1) mandatory opaque resume token on every paged response, 2) optional resume-offset integer inside token to support partial chunk resumption, 3) Idempotency-Key header accepted on stream/unary calls, server may allow replay within replay_window_ms.

sam: main design Q: should resume semantics be encoded in HTTP headers or in body? headers feel cleaner for streaming.

anya: headers look fine. But language surfaces differ: Python async iterators expect raising on unrecoverable, TS streaming prefers returning done. We should standardize surface mapping in SDKs: server contract stays the same, SDK flavors map to idiomatic errors/values.

kevin: agreed. Proposal for SDK mapping:
- Python: raise ResumeNeededError with resume_token attr when server returns 409/resume-needed; caller can call client.resume(resume_token) or pass token to generator.
- TS: iterator yields { done: false, resumeToken } event or throw, but prefer uniform event api.
- Go: return (items, nextToken, err) where err==ResumeNeededError and nextToken set.

liz: small nit: let's avoid putting secrets or user ids in resume tokens. Opaque only. If we need sequence numbers, store them inside signed token or server metadata, not plain text.

maria: exactly. token format note in RFC: base64(signed_json) with fields {cursor_id, offset?, seq?:int, exp:ts}. Clients must treat token as opaque string.

sam: tradeoffs: including offset reduces server-side ambiguity for partial chunk reads but makes tokens larger and slightly harder to rotate. If we keep offset out, server must map cursor->stream position on resume which can be heavier.

anya: also think about retries/backoff semantics: SDKs should retry idempotent calls automatically (unary/list) but not auto-retry partial stream resumes unless resume token present. Backoff: exponential with jitter, max 10s.

kevin: concrete header examples for transport handshake:
```
X-Resume-Token: <opaque>
Idempotency-Key: <uuid>
X-Resume-Offset: <optional-int>   # servers may ignore
```
Server responses: 200 with body + `resume_token` field OR 409 + `resume_token` header if resume required.

liz: can we add `Retry-After-ms` in the 429/503 responses so SDKs can honor server load windows?

maria: yes — RFC includes `Retry-After-MS`. Also servers should include `replay_window_ms` in initial connection meta so SDKs know how long a resume token stays valid.

kevin: interoperability note: Go gRPC vs HTTP/JSON — for gRPC streaming we'll put resume_token in the first trailing metadata entry and accept idempotency-key as metadata. For HTTP JSON, headers as above and token in JSON body for paged unary responses.

sam: error handling checklist for SDKs: map transport errors -> ResumeNeededError / TransientError / PermanentError. Provide a small helper `client.resume_stream(token)` that returns a new iterator starting at token.

anya: tests we need: cross-language replay test that intentionally cuts connection mid-chunk and asserts no duplicates beyond N tokens. Also test rotation of keys and expired tokens.

maria: ops: @deploy-bot can you canary handshake-v0 on staging for python/ts SDKs? want to validate token shape + Retry-After behavior.

deploy-bot: canary deployed handshake-v0 to staging at 2024-11-14T14:05Z. Route: /v1/streams (canary). Metrics: resume_token emit rate 0.2% so far.

kevin: next steps: I'll draft a tiny example in the SDK repo showing `for await (const item of client.stream()) {}` -> how to surface resume token in TS idiomatic way.

maria: thanks — I'll update the RFC with the offsets/discussed header names and add the replay_window_ms field. If anyone objects to any of the above call it out here. :thinking:

liz: looks good to me.

sam: +1

anya: +1

maria: great — target to land the RFC updates EOD and open issues for SDK mapping.
